lawFindings.issue: The paid add-on is pre-selected and charged unless the consumer unticks it, so there is no express consent to the extra payment and the consumer can claim it back.
The trader may raise the price at any time, at its discretion and without notice, so the consumer is charged the higher fee before being able to leave; a likely unfair term.
A EUR 25 charge on withdrawal: the trader must refund all payments and the consumer bears no cost for withdrawing beyond what the Directive allows.

The service is supplied as it stands with no conformity promise and a one-month credit as the only remedy, which excludes the mandatory conformity requirements and remedies (repair, price reduction, termination).

All uploaded files are erased on the day the contract ends with no way to retrieve them; the consumer must be able to get their content back free of charge, and a cloud storage provider must allow at least a 30-day data retrieval period.
Sharing personal data with partners for their advertising relies on a consent bundled into the subscription that cannot be withdrawn, so it is not freely given or revocable and has no lawful basis.
An exclusive Dublin forum agreed before any dispute stops a consumer living in Portugal, a country the trader directs its service to, from suing in her home courts.

lawfulClauses.why: A consumer who asked for the service to start during the withdrawal period and then withdraws pays a proportionate amount for what was provided.

Updates for a stated valid reason, at no extra cost, explained clearly, with 30 days' advance notice and a free right to terminate within 30 days if the change is detrimental, meet the conditions for modifying a digital service.
Parties may choose the governing law of a consumer contract as long as the consumer keeps the mandatory protection of the law of their habitual residence, which the clause preserves.

notCovered.why: Whether heirs can access a deceased person's account and files is a question of national succession law; the included EU acts do not answer it.

otherMistakes.issue: 12 x EUR 9.99 is EUR 119.88, not EUR 129.88.
Refers to a procedure in clause 11.2, but the agreement has no clause 11.
The trader signs as Lumenvault Cloud Ltd, but the party named in the agreement is Lumenvault Ltd.

lawFindings.issue: A nine-month trial period exceeds the six-month maximum probation and is disproportionate for a twelve-month fixed-term assignment.
Back-to-back shifts with eight hours off breach the 11 consecutive hours of daily rest, and no compensatory rest is given, so no derogation can apply.
The agency worker is paid less than the client's own staff in the same job; agency workers must get at least the basic pay they would get if hired directly by the user undertaking.
Paid annual leave is replaced by a percentage added to weekly pay with unpaid days off; the minimum paid leave cannot be replaced by an allowance during the employment.
Training the worker must have by law is charged to the worker and not paid; mandatory training must be free of cost and count as working time.
A EUR 2,500 release fee for taking a direct job with the client deters a later direct hire and charges the worker a fee, both prohibited for temporary-work agencies.
Ending the contract because the worker becomes pregnant is less favourable treatment related to pregnancy, which is sex discrimination including in dismissals.

lawfulClauses.why: Single weeks of up to 54 hours are allowed when average weekly working time, overtime included, stays within 48 hours over a reference period of up to four months.
Side jobs outside the schedule are allowed; the only restriction rests on an objective ground (protecting business confidentiality and avoiding conflicts of interest).
Calculating a part-time worker's pay and allowances in proportion to hours worked applies the pro rata temporis principle and is not less favourable treatment.

notCovered.why: Sick pay levels and unpaid waiting days are set by national law and collective agreements; no included EU act regulates them.

otherMistakes.issue: 38 hours x EUR 15.20 is EUR 577.60, not EUR 592.80.
Refers to clause 12.3, but the contract ends at clause 9.
The worker signs as Agnieszka Novak, but the party named in the contract is Agnieszka Nowak.

lawFindings.issue: A sale made at the buyer's home must come with the three-business-day cancellation notice and forms; declaring the sale final and the deposit non-refundable denies that right.
Credit is conditioned on repayment by preauthorized automatic debits from the buyer's account.
Requiring the spouse to co-sign only because the applicant is married, regardless of the applicant's own creditworthiness, is credit discrimination on marital status.
A nonpossessory lien on furniture and appliances the buyer already owns is a non-purchase-money security interest in household goods, an unfair credit practice.
The contract lacks the holder notice and makes the buyer keep paying an assignee even if the goods fail, cutting off the buyer's claims and defenses against any holder.
A supplier that gives a written warranty may not disclaim implied warranties; selling the rest AS IS with no implied promise of quality or fitness is ineffective and prohibited.

A collection agency may not discuss the debt with the employer, relatives or neighbors, or call at work, without consent given directly to the collector; a term in the original credit contract does not supply that.

lawfulClauses.why: A security interest in the goods being bought is a purchase-money security interest, which the Credit Practices Rule allows even for household goods.
A written agreement to arbitrate disputes from a transaction in commerce is valid and enforceable; it keeps small claims court available and leaves warranty claims out.
Electronic signatures and records are valid when the consumer consents after the required disclosures and shows they can open the electronic records.

notCovered.why: Self-help repossession and entering the buyer's home to take back collateral are governed by state law (UCC Article 9 and breach-of-the-peace rules), not by the included federal acts.

otherMistakes.issue: The total of payments should be USD 4,159.08 (Amount Financed USD 3,200.00 plus Finance Charge USD 959.08, and 36 x USD 115.53), not USD 4,259.08.
The first payment is due on July 22, 2026, a month before the contract date of August 22, 2026.
The buyer signs as David Okafor, but the buyer named in the contract is Daniel Okafor.
